old: At its root sits a Latin word for leaning on something, or someone.
The person who depends on you for service traces back to that same idea of leaning.
It shares an ancestor with the Latin verb clinare — to lean.
clues: This noun names a kind of person in a working relationship, and it traces back to a Latin word akin to a verb meaning "to lean."
It is someone who pays a professional such as a lawyer, accountant or therapist for services, a more personal and ongoing tie than a shopper who is simply a customer.
In computing, it is the program or device that asks a server for data, like the email app on your phone.
